title: Reuters: Russia's gasoline output falls to about 70% of domestic demand
detail: Russia's gasoline production fell to roughly 70% of domestic consumption by late August, Reuters reported, citing industry sources, after a wave of drone attacks forced refineries in Perm, Nizhny Novgorod, Yaroslavl and elsewhere to suspend operations. Average August output ran around 90,000 tonnes/day (about 80% of estimated summer demand of 115,000 tonnes/day), but the latest emergency shutdowns widened the daily production-demand gap to roughly 35,000 tonnes, with current output near 80,000 tonnes/day. Russia is leaning on imports to close the gap: seaborne gasoline from Asia is expected to total about 270,000 tonnes in August, alongside roughly 150,000 tonnes from Belarus.

media.caption: Russia's gasoline output fell to about 70% of domestic demand by late August 2026 after renewed refinery drone strikes, Reuters reported

title: Russia extends producer diesel export ban through September 30
detail: The Russian government extended its ban on diesel, marine fuel and gasoil exports by fuel producers through September 30, 2026, industry sources said, as domestic shortages persisted. The measure — which had run from July 8 through August 31 — sits alongside separate restrictions already in force: a ban on diesel exports by non-producers and motor gasoline through January 31, 2027, and on jet fuel through November 30, 2026. Officials said the extension was meant 'to stabilize the domestic fuel market' after repeated Ukrainian drone strikes kept refineries offline; Deputy PM Alexander Novak said the government had not yet decided on lifting the ban and maintained there was no domestic diesel shortage, even as several refineries resumed operations.

media.caption: Russia extends its producer diesel export ban through September 30, 2026 amid persistent domestic shortages
